summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with a history of endometriosis, bipolar disorder, and chronic pelvic pain was admitted for an acute flare of left pelvic pain, consistent with prior episodes. She presented with severe pain and inability to tolerate oral intake but showed no signs of infection or acute abdominal pathology. Labs revealed a transient lactate elevation that resolved with hydration and pain control. Anemia was noted with a hemoglobin drop from 11.9 to 9.9 g/dL, likely due to chronic blood loss from menstruation, and iron deficiency was previously confirmed. She was managed with IV fluids, reinitiation of her home pain regimen, and monitoring. Gynecology recommended continuing her current medications and proceeding with a scheduled colonoscopy to evaluate for rectal endometriosis before surgical planning. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged.
